data.description:
BUILDPLAN.md T-14 (M3).

Bank format (`SPEC.md` §3.1–3.3) and migration of the eight MVP questions: verified facts carried over **as `legacy` records — only the fields the MVP wrote, nothing back-filled** (`SPEC.md` §3.2, D-16), the MVP's `error_codes` renamed to `compile_error_code` on q8's record, `explains` three beats and `trace` drafted for organizer affirmation, `explanation` kept as `legacy`

Criteria: AC-13, AC-17, AC-73, AC-87
Harness hooks: see EVALUATION.md rows for those IDs; `just test` is the inner loop (≤ 60 s).
Depends on (BUILDPLAN): T-01
BUILDPLAN notes: **Only q3 migrates as authored** (touchpoint T-22, D-15). q4, q7 and q8 fit as programs but their options must be re-authored to one line of at most 29 characters and re-verified (the machine decides the new answer). q1, q2, q5 and q6 exceed the wall's 7-line capacity at the guessed room and stay in the MVP bank only, until re-authored or until the rehearsal's measurements raise the capacity.

Orchestrator notes: Only q3 migrates as authored (D-15). Never write down what a program prints: legacy records carry only what `mvp/2026-08-12/verified.json` holds, nothing back-filled.

Workflow mode: inline-full. Terminal pre-merge status: review. PR base: origin/main.
Standing clauses: criteria outrank SPEC on behaviour, state, payloads and copy; SPEC outranks the prototype, which wins on visual detail only. Never write down what a program prints. Answer position is a uniform draw from the date, never balanced. Miri proves absence of UB on executed paths only. Colour is never the only signal. Code never causes horizontal page scroll. Never `git add -A`. Signing goes through 1Password: retry once, then escalate.

Plan: filled in by the delegator's plan phase.

data.body: READY PQ-18 CWD /Users/michellerojas/rust-nyc-pop-quiz-worktrees/bank-format HEAD 2ab95e31b78ee48a7067dc47904e98b28baf3d37 BASE 2ab95e31b78ee48a7067dc47904e98b28baf3d37 MODE active

ORCHESTRATOR RULING: where the ticket text and your boot brief differ, the brief governs (it is later and knows about PR #8). PR base is ai-c11-cc/repo-scaffold until #8 merges; fly, push and PR commands run in your tab with the client's approval. The worktree .claude/settings.json now also allows sandboxed writes to /Users/michellerojas/rust-nyc-pop-quiz/.lattice, so lattice commands should no longer need the bypass; git fetch/push over SSH still do.

ORCHESTRATOR: PR #8 merged to main at 0742d35 (merge commit; your base commit 2ab95e3 is its second parent). From now on: rebase onto origin/main (git fetch origin && git rebase origin/main; it should be a no-op or trivial), and open your PR against main, not ai-c11-cc/repo-scaffold. Drop the 'Based on #8' line from the PR body.

CONTRACT DEFECT (reported, not fixed) — a does-not-compile question can never be affirmed, so it can never be scheduled. SPEC 7.4 requires a trace of at least two steps before affirm; SPEC 3.1 and D-10 require the trace's last step to be the one whose values names stdout; SPEC 3.2 says a does-not-compile record has no stdout. The two rules have no satisfiable joint form for that class. Not hypothetical: q8 is one, AC-11 has the generator produce them, AC-24 puts 'does not compile' on every question, D-22 gives the class its own receipt, and BUILDPLAN's minimum viable cut expects q8 in the October bank. T-18 inherits the unsatisfiable gate (G-12 makes it blocking). PQ-18 implements the narrowest honest reading for its own validation only — the stdout invariant binds a non-empty trace on a record that ran — and edits no contract file. Routing is yours.

ORCHESTRATOR: defect confirmed and routed upstream to tone-architect as amendment F-15 (recorded in .lattice/orchestration/run-state.md and sequence/run-state.md). Your reading stands for this ticket: the stdout invariant binds a non-empty trace on a record that ran; a does-not-compile question's trace ends on the step that names the compiler's refusal. Proceed to implement; do not change q8's trace shape to satisfy 7.4 by invention — leave it with the MVP text drafted as far as it goes and a review note. The affirm gate itself is T-18's and will receive the amended rule.

BASE CHANGE PQ-18 — PR #8 merged mid-plan as 0742d35 and the remote branch ai-c11-cc/repo-scaffold was pruned. git ls-remote lists refs/heads/main only, and merge-base confirms main carries the scaffold commit 2ab95e31. Rebased onto origin/main (fast-forward, no commits of my own yet). The PR will target main directly: no stacking, no 'Based on #8' line, and no retarget for you to do. The press-ahead premise in my boot prompt has expired rather than been wrong.

BLOCKED PQ-18 — commit signing. The work is complete and green; nothing is committed. 'git commit' fails with 'error: 1Password: failed to fill whole buffer' / 'fatal: failed to write commit object'. First attempt failed inside the sandbox with 'Could not connect to socket' (a sandbox denial on the agent socket); two further attempts outside the sandbox both failed with the buffer error, so the agent is reachable and the signing operation itself is failing — 1Password is most likely locked and wants the operator to unlock or approve the key. Per standing clause 5 I have not disabled or bypassed signing and have stopped here. State: branch ai-c11-cc/bank-format at origin/main 0742d35 with zero commits; all deliverables written and staged-or-unstaged in the worktree; 'just test' green warm at 0.66s (140 pipeline tests, room canary, web layout). Unblock is one operator action: unlock 1Password, then I commit, review, validate and open the PR against main.

SIGNING RETRY FAILED (third distinct error) — staying needs_human, staging untouched. Attempt 1 (sandboxed): 'Could not connect to socket. Is the agent running?'. Attempts 2 and 3 (outside the sandbox): 'failed to fill whole buffer'. Attempt 4 (outside the sandbox, just now): 'error: 1Password: agent returned an error'. Three different failure modes from the same agent suggests the item or key is not being released to op-ssh-sign for this worktree, not a transient socket problem. git config is unchanged and correct: commit.gpgsign=true, gpg.format=ssh, signingkey ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIKfJClLrxphY1n8PbDB0h5Dx. I have not touched signing config and have not attempted --no-gpg-sign. Branch ai-c11-cc/bank-format is at 0742d35 (origin/main) with zero commits. Index holds commit 1 of 4 fully staged; the other three are unstaged/untracked in the worktree, deliberately left as-is. The exact four 'git add' lists and commit messages are in the delegator tab for the client to run from a normal terminal. just test remains green warm at 0.66s.

DONE PQ-18 PR https://github.com/mrojas54/rust-nyc-pop-quiz/pull/10 HEAD b4d946c9baf07c0e833c0b084ffec8a63a8ad7cd BASE 0742d3578726e3e0486c7b3793c6bb934e3e8579 (origin/main) test-warm 0.66s

PR state OPEN, MERGEABLE, base main, head sha differs from base sha, body stored (7722 chars) and verified. CI green: gh-wait-runs 1/1 succeeded on the head sha. Five signed commits, every one verifying Good "git" signature with SHA256:ZmDAi3no4K32bND+82CGabBv2D2VGJ7CsBZHH1MV5c4. Code review PASS-WITH-NITS on 9745025 with no Critical and no Major; both findings accepted and fixed in b4d946c. Validation and Code review both attached as notes.

deviations:
1. The receipt's cases are published under bank/fixtures/receipts/ so T-05's JavaScript twin tests the same files. The contract says one function; two languages need it, and one shared fixture set is how the build keeps them one.
2. why_tempting is carried on Option rather than under explains (SPEC 3.1 files it under explains). A beat keyed by letter dangles when the date draws a different slot — the prototype keyed one to "A" — and a beat keyed by position silently mis-attaches on the first reorder. Recorded in bank/README.md and in the schema.
3. correct is a derived function, not a stored field. SPEC 3.1 lists it as a field but marks it derived (G-2); a field is something a person can edit, and AC-7 exists to catch exactly that edit.
4. The re-authoring note goes in review.reason with status unset. No new field minted; reason's reader per SPEC 3.1 is the generator's next run, which is who needs to know the option rule.
5. receipt_detail returns facts, not take-it-home's strings. AC-87's 'not recorded' and 'run separately' are participant-facing copy on a surface T-12 renders and T-22 freezes; SPEC 11 does not hold them, so this ticket derives the facts and does not author the words.
6. The schema is enforced by a two-directional drift test, not a validator. No JSON-Schema validator in the standard library and pyproject.toml is serialized to another ticket. bank/README.md says so plainly so nobody assumes records are validated against it at runtime. Flagged for T-19.
7. Seven of nine receipt fixtures are synthetic, describe no Rust program, and each says so in its own text, following tests/fixtures/scaffold-placeholder.json's precedent. A judgment call against the house rule, made openly.
8. '✓ Ran ‹N› times' renders SPEC 7.5's template literally, so at N=1 it reads 'Ran 1 times'. Inventing a singular would be authoring participant-facing copy that belongs to SPEC 11 and T-22's freeze.
9. The MVP's stderr_head is not carried. A real machine artifact, but SPEC 3.2 does not list it and compile_error_code is what the receipt reads. Dropped rather than smuggled in under an invented key.
10. q4, q7 and q8 migrate with an empty trace. The MVP holds no step structure for them and their options are about to be re-authored, so a trace drafted now would be drafted against text that will not exist; an empty trace also correctly blocks affirm.
11. quoted_outputs applies no shape filter. Reading the eight August explanations, both obvious filters fail: 'created' (q2) is printed output AND a valid Rust identifier, and [0] (q8, from &v[0]) is bracketed and is not output. AC-73 blocks acceptance, so a false positive costs an organizer a question. The decision goes to T-18, which has the verified output and a reviewer looking at it.
12. Deviation 5 from my earlier plan (PR base ai-c11-cc/repo-scaffold) is WITHDRAWN — PR #8 merged mid-plan, so this targets main directly. No retarget needed.

notes for the Orchestrator:
A. CONTRACT DEFECT, unresolved and yours to route (also sent separately). A does-not-compile question can never be affirmed, so it can never be scheduled. SPEC 7.4 needs two trace steps before affirm; SPEC 3.1 and D-10 need the trace's last step to name stdout; SPEC 3.2 says such a record has no stdout. q8 is one, AC-11 has the generator produce them, AC-24 puts 'does not compile' on every question, D-22 gives the class its own receipt, and BUILDPLAN's minimum viable cut expects q8 in the October bank. T-18 inherits an affirm gate a whole class of question cannot satisfy. I implemented the narrowest honest reading for this ticket's validation only and edited no contract file.
B. SIGNING. op-ssh-sign failed four times here with three distinct errors. The path that worked, and that I used per invocation and never wrote to config: git -c gpg.ssh.program=ssh-keygen commit with SSH_AUTH_SOCK pointing at the 1Password agent socket. Worth putting in the next delegator's boot prompt.
C. FOR T-19. bank.py exports MAX_OPTION_LINE_CHARS, MAX_OPTION_LINES and options_needing_reauthoring so bank-audit and the migration's review notes cannot disagree about which options fail D-15. The source program's fit is not measured anywhere yet.
D. FOR T-17. bank/history.json holds version 1 with three empty stores and History.sizes()/total() for AC-17's visibility half. source_hash normalizes nothing, deliberately, so AC-14's exact rejection and AC-15's normalized rejection stay distinguishable.
E. FOR T-15b. A legacy record is replaced whole, never merged (D-16). append_question refuses to overwrite, so re-verification must write deliberately rather than append.
F. q4 and q7 need new programs, not just new option text, because their correct option fails D-15 and an option's text must equal what the program printed. q8 needs one distractor replaced and keeps its answer. Each record's review.reason says which.
